arxiv-2106-06669.title: Spatial Bayesian GLM on the cortical surface produces reliable task activations in individuals and groups
arxiv-2106-06669.creator: Daniel Spencer, Yu (Ryan) Yue, David Bolin, Sarah Ryan, Amanda F. Mejia
arxiv-2106-06669.description: Abstract The general linear model (GLM) is a widely popular and convenient tool for estimating the functional brain response and identifying areas of significant activation during a task or stimulus. However, the classical GLM is based on a massive univariate approach that does not explicitly leverage the similarity of activation patterns among neighboring brain locations.

arxiv-2211-00956.title: Inhomogeneous Defect Distribution in Mixed-Polytype Metal Halide Perovskites
arxiv-2211-00956.creator: Young Won Woo, Zhenzhu Li, Young-Kwang Jung, Ji-Sang Park, Aron Walsh
arxiv-2211-00956.description: Abstract The competition between corner, edge and face-sharing octahedral networks is a cause of phase inhomogeneity in metal halide perovskite thin-films. Here we probe the charged iodine vacancy distribution and transport at the junction between cubic and hexagonal polytypes of CsPbI 3 from first-principles materials modelling.

arxiv-2212-01934.title: Computing a Dirichlet domain for a hyperbolic surface
arxiv-2212-01934.creator: Vincent Despré, Benedikt Kolbe, Hugo Parlier, Monique Teillaud
arxiv-2212-01934.description: Abstract The goal of this paper is to exhibit and analyze an algorithm that takes a given closed orientable hyperbolic surface and outputs an explicit Dirichlet domain. The input is a fundamental polygon with side pairings. While grounded in topological considerations, the algorithm makes key use of the geometry of the surface.

arxiv-2305-06949.title: Twisted bilayer graphene at charge neutrality: competing orders of SU(4) Dirac fermions
arxiv-2305-06949.creator: Nikolaos Parthenios, Laura Classen
arxiv-2305-06949.description: Abstract We study possible patterns for spontaneous symmetry breaking in a Dirac fermion model, which is applicable to twisted bilayer graphene at charge neutrality. We show how a chiral SU(4) symmetry emerges and construct the corresponding low-energy model that includes a Fierz-complete set of symmetry-allowed four-fermion interactions.

arxiv-2305-14689.title: Least Squares Regression Can Exhibit Under-Parameterized Double Descent
arxiv-2305-14689.creator: Xinyue Li, Rishi Sonthalia
arxiv-2305-14689.description: Abstract The relationship between the number of training data points, the number of parameters, and the generalization capabilities of models has been widely studied. Previous work has shown that double descent can occur in the over-parameterized regime and that the standard bias-variance trade-off holds in the under-parameterized regime. These works provide multiple reasons for the existence of the peak.

arxiv-2308-01084.title: Data-Driven Identification of Quadratic Representations for Nonlinear Hamiltonian Systems using Weakly Symplectic Liftings
arxiv-2308-01084.creator: Süleyman Yıldız, Pawan Goyal, Thomas Bendokat, Peter Benner
arxiv-2308-01084.description: Abstract We present a framework for learning Hamiltonian systems using data. This work is based on a lifting hypothesis, which posits that nonlinear Hamiltonian systems can be written as nonlinear systems with cubic Hamiltonians. By leveraging this, we obtain quadratic dynamics that are Hamiltonian in a transformed coordinate system.

arxiv-2312-03216.title: SDSRA: A Skill-Driven Skill-Recombination Algorithm for Efficient Policy Learning
arxiv-2312-03216.creator: Eric H. Jiang, Andrew Lizarraga
arxiv-2312-03216.description: Abstract In this paper we introduce a novel algorithm-the Skill-Driven Skill Recombination Algorithm (SDSRA)—an innovative framework that significantly enhances the efficiency of achieving maximum entropy in reinforcement learning tasks. We find that SDSRA achieves faster convergence compared to the traditional Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm and produces improved policies.

arxiv-2405-09525.title: Improved classical shadows from local symmetries in the Schur basis
arxiv-2405-09525.creator: Daniel Grier, Sihan Liu, Gaurav Mahajan
arxiv-2405-09525.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel Grier, Sihan Liu, Gaurav Mahajan. We study the sample complexity of the classical shadows task: what is the fewest number of copies of an unknown state you need to measure to predict expected values with respect to some class of observables? Large joint measurements are likely required in order to minimize sample complexity, but previous joint measurement protocols only work when the unknown state is pure.

arxiv-2408-11341.title: EHL*: Memory-Budgeted Indexing for Ultrafast Optimal Euclidean Pathfinding
arxiv-2408-11341.creator: Jinchun Du, Bojie Shen, Muhammad Aamir Cheema
arxiv-2408-11341.description: Abstract The Euclidean Shortest Path Problem (ESPP), which involves finding the shortest path in a Euclidean plane with polygonal obstacles, is a classic problem with numerous real-world applications. The current state-of-the-art solution, Euclidean Hub Labeling (EHL), offers ultra-fast query performance, outperforming existing techniques by 1-2 orders of magnitude in runtime efficiency.

arxiv-2408-17273.title: Overlapping subspaces and singular systems with application to Isogeometric Analysis
arxiv-2408-17273.creator: Andrea Bressan
arxiv-2408-17273.description: Abstract We propose a framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) motivated by isogeometric analysis (IGA) and local tensor-product splines. Instead of using a global basis for the solution space we use as generators the disjoint union of subspace bases. This leads to a potentially singular linear system, which is handled by a Krylov linear solver.

arxiv-2412-11999.title: Pattern-avoiding shallow permutations
arxiv-2412-11999.creator: Kassie Archer, Aaron Geary, Robert P. Laudone
arxiv-2412-11999.description: Abstract Shallow permutations were defined in 1977 to be those that satisfy the lower bound of the Diaconis-Graham inequality. Recently, there has been renewed interest in these permutations. In particular, Berman and Tenner showed they satisfy certain pattern avoidance conditions in their cycle form and Woo showed they are exactly those whose cycle diagrams are unlinked.

arxiv-2502-07756.title: Nonabelian Yang–Mills–Higgs and Plateau’s problem in codimension three
arxiv-2502-07756.creator: Davide Parise, Alessandro Pigati, Daniel Stern
arxiv-2502-07756.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Davide Parise, Alessandro Pigati, Daniel Stern. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the SU ⁡ ( 2 ) \SU(2) -Yang–Mills–Higgs energy E ⁡ ( Φ , A ) = ∫ M | d A ​ Φ | 2 + | F A | 2 E(\Phi,A)=\int_{M}|d_{A}\Phi|^{2}+|F_{A}|^{2} in the large mass limit, proving convergence to the codimension-three area functional in the sense of De Giorgi’s Γ \Gamma -convergence.

arxiv-2503-17899.title: What Time Tells Us? An Explorative Study of Time Awareness Learned from Static Images
arxiv-2503-17899.creator: Dongheng Lin, Han Hu, Jianbo Jiao { d.lin.2@, hxh347@student, j.jiao@}bham.ac.uk
arxiv-2503-17899.description: Abstract Time becomes visible through illumination changes in what we see. Inspired by this, in this paper we explore the potential to learn time awareness from static images, trying to answer: what time tells us? To this end, we first introduce a Time-Oriented Collection (TOC) dataset, which contains 130,906 images with reliable timestamps.

arxiv-2506-06175.title: Does It Run and Is That Enough ? Revisiting Text-to-Chart Generation with a Multi-Agent Approach
arxiv-2506-06175.creator: James Ford, Anthony Rios
arxiv-2506-06175.description: Abstract Large language models can translate natural-language chart descriptions into runnable code, yet approximately 15% of the generated scripts still fail to execute, even after supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. We investigate whether this persistent error rate stems from model limitations or from reliance on a single-prompt design.

pmc-12362928.creator: Esraa Abdellatif Hammouda, Rasha Ashmawy, Mahmoud A Hassan, Ramy Mohamed Ghazy
pmc-12362928.description: BackgroundAssessing quality of life (QoL) of caregivers of patients with tuberculosis (TB) highlights their unseen sacrifices. This study aimed to address the domains of QoL of TB caregivers and to estimate their possible determinants in Alexandria, Egypt.MethodsThis cross-sectional survey was conducted in the chest clinics and the main chest hospital in Alexandria, Egypt.

pmc-12500236.title: Chemoselective Characterization of New Extracellular Matrix Deposition in Bioengineered Tumor Tissues
pmc-12500236.creator: Zihan Ling, Burke Niego, Qingyang Li, Dhruv Bhattaram, Vanessa Serna Villa, Michael Hu, Zhuowei Gong, Lloyd M Smith, Brian L Frey, Xi Ren
pmc-12500236.description: In both native and engineered tissues, the extracellular matrix (ECM) supports and regulates nearly all aspects of cellular pathophysiology, and in response, cells extensively remodel their surrounding extracellular environments through new ECM protein deposition. Understanding this intricate bi‐directional cell‐ECM interaction is key to tissue engineering, but it remains challenging to investigate.

pmc-12754990.title: Spatial bayesian modeling of diabetes mellitus (DM) risk in the United States
pmc-12754990.creator: Moses Asori, Kadae Phimia, Eric Dellmelle, Deborah SK Thomas
pmc-12754990.description: BackgroundSpatial targeting of disease burden has long been instrumental to achieving optimal health resource allocation in the United States (US). Building on a previous study, the current research examined the spatial variation and hotspots of Diabetes Mellitus (DM) risk across the US.

pmc-13154236.title: Advancements in Retinitis Pigmentosa: The Path Toward Personalized Treatment and Vision Restoration
pmc-13154236.creator: Komal, Lovekesh Singh, Subrahmanya Sarma Ganti
pmc-13154236.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). to provide either limited reviews of specific therapeutic developments or general descriptive surveys that do not involve any critical appraisal [1]. An integrated and multimodal approach to RP management can be proposed as a system-based approach to individual treatment. We are striving to integrate the knowledge gained in molecular genetics, imaging tools, non-genetic treatments, and individualized diagnostics into a coordinated approach that facilitates clinical translation and patient stratification [2].

pmc-13371015.title: Polyubiquitination and accumulation of PEG10 regulated by SIAH1/2 affiliates the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-13371015.creator: Zhiyi Liu, Qing Luo, Qinghe Hu, Kai Wu, Jun Sun, Nan Xia, Jiawei Xu, Kuan Cao, Hengliang Shi, Bin Zhang
pmc-13371015.description: BackgroundSIAH1 and SIAH2 are key regulators of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) initiation and progression, but their precise molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Although both interact with the oncoprotein PEG10, it is unknown whether PEG10 mediates their regulatory effects on HCC or what the underlying mechanisms are.

pmc-13539457.title: Evolving conservation: The role of unconventional approaches to restore contemporary vertebrate populations and genomic biodiversity
pmc-13539457.creator: Bridgett M vonHoldt, Matt James, Stephen J Gaughran, Alexandra L DeCandia, Klaus-Peter Koepfli, Dan Flores, Nucharin Songsasen, Kristin E Brzeski, Evelyn L Jensen
pmc-13539457.description: Conservation biology and restoration ecology are two essential yet distinct disciplines that address the growing challenge of biodiversity loss. Traditionally, these fields have relied on ecological principles and management practices aimed at protecting or reestablishing natural systems. The crisis is no longer just ecological; it is evolutionary and genomic.
